tweets.text:
I look at what I do with Fable 5.2 in the cracks of my week and think: this would've taken five people and $200,000.

Then I look at what my team does with the same AI.

Last week, between meetings, I analyzed our customer survey, made a game for our team, spotted an opportunity to sell @Every to teams, built a CRM, and started reaching out.

Look at that and you might ask: Why would I need a team at all?

The chart seems to agree. On OpenAI's GDPval benchmark, AI went from beating human experts 12.4% of the time in 2024 to around 83% in 2026. That's the aggregate view of the future of work: gather a lot of data and extrapolate a trend line.

But the aggregate misses something. To see it, you have to get intimate: zoom in on one real situation, with all its messiness, and extrapolate from there.

We gave everyone at Every access to the same customer survey and the same AI models.

• I found an opportunity to sell to teams.
• @poojary_yash saw that first-time subscribers were churning because we send too much email.
• @dabrundage noticed that many of our readers feel lonely: they're excited about AI, but people around them think they're crazy.
• @jackcheng turned the results into a Claymation game show.

Could you ask Claude to produce what each of them found? Maybe. But generating possibilities is cheap. Knowing which ones matter is hard.

@hammer_mt ran an experiment to predict what I'd say in Slack. When Claude got 400 attempts, it produced an answer like mine 93% of the time. But when it had to rank its own answers, mine landed in its top 10% only around 60% of the time.

Each person on a team is responsible for a different part of the world. That responsibility narrows where they look, and their perspective helps them decide what matters enough to act on. A team explores more possibilities than a single default prompt, and it can take responsibility for what it finds.

The obvious objection: models will get better at ranking. I think they will. But people aren't frozen while that happens. Comparing 2026 Yash with 2027 Claude misses that there will also be a 2027 Yash, with another year of experience, using 2027 Claude.

As models improve and spread, they raise the floor for everyone. The default answer becomes the baseline. The value is in using your perspective and responsibility to push past it.

That's why I think we need to change how we measure AI. Instead of only asking how well a model performs on problems everyone agrees are worth solving, ask: How good is it at doing my work, from my perspective?

The aggregate can show us the capability curve. The intimate helps us see what we might build, and who we might become, as we ride it.

I presented this at Thesis: 2027. The full talk is on the Every podcast:
tweets.summary_en: AI lets individuals accomplish far more, but teams remain valuable because people identify different meaningful insights from the same information. Generating possibilities is cheap; judging which ones matter remains difficult, including for AI ranking its own outputs.

tweets.text:
It has been such a pleasure to partner with Rox from the earliest days.

I have also learnt a lot about what it means to run a company at AI-pace from @ishanmkh. His talk at our recent founder retreat was incredible. https://t.co/UdZlqzZetx

There are basically two kinds of companies to build right now.

1. Diffusion of AI
This is the "vertical SaaS" of today. There are a bunch of different models for it (FDE company, rollup, horizontal product) but ultimately it all boils down to the same thing: get AI diffused very close to where the work is being done.

Profound, Cognition, Harvey etc. A lot of great companies will get built here.

2. Frontier of AI
This is where the really interesting action is. Use AI to accelerate scientific progress, then build products from that progress.

It is a harder category to see. But we are seeing a lot more of it at @spc:

- Externa is adding hundreds of new chemical building blocks to proteins, so you can engineer a drug to match the disease instead of settling for what nature gave you.

- Epana Bio is using genomics and AI to design autoimmune therapies that go after the cellular origin of the disease.

- VenomicsAI is doing AI-accelerated drug discovery from venoms.

- Equivariant is doing multi-physics modeling for the semiconductor industry.

(There are always picks-and-shovels for AI as well. Lots of amazing companies in that category.)

Category 2 is not well understood or much talked about externally. It should be because I think that is where the vast majority of model driven returns will come from.
tweets.summary_en: AI startups broadly fall into two categories: bringing AI into existing workflows and using AI to advance science and build products from new discoveries. The argument is that the second category, spanning drug discovery and semiconductor modeling, is underappreciated and could capture most model-driven returns.

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary_en: Shows how Mariko Mori used Claude to write code for a computer-generated animation presented as a new video installation in her retrospective.
builders.summary_zh: 展示森万里子如何使用 Claude 编写计算机生成动画的代码，并将其作为回顾展中的新影像装置呈现。

keywords.definition_zh: 在艺术语境中指回顾艺术家一段时期创作历程的展览。
keywords.example_zh: 这里指 Mariko Mori 的「All That Shines」回顾展，她在展览中呈现了借助 Claude 编写代码制作的新作品。

keywords.definition_zh: 通过计算机程序或图形技术生成的动画。
keywords.example_zh: 推文说 Claude 帮助编写了生成动画的代码，没有说明动画画面是由生成式 AI 直接生成的。

keywords.definition_zh: 以影像为核心媒介、结合展览空间呈现的装置艺术。
keywords.example_zh: 这段计算机生成的动画最终作为新的影像装置在回顾展中展出。

tweets.text: Mariko Mori has pushed the boundaries of art for three decades. For her retrospective "All That Shines," she used Claude to write code for a computer-generated animation, presented as a new video installation. https://t.co/MtJ1rlClxt

podcasts.name: AI & I by Every
podcasts.title: A New Vision for Human Work After Automation
podcasts.summary_en: Introduces a discussion of how everyday AI use is changing work and references Every's first conference in Brooklyn. The supplied transcript ends before any substantive findings or speaker arguments appear.
podcasts.summary_zh: 开场提出探讨日常 AI 使用如何改变工作，并提及 Every 在布鲁克林举办的首场会议。所给逐字稿在具体发现或嘉宾观点出现前便已结束。

vocab.definition_zh: 令人震惊的；令人愤慨的；极其糟糕的。
vocab.example_en: The investigation revealed appalling working conditions.
vocab.example_zh: 调查揭露了令人震惊的工作条件。

vocab.definition_en: A person or organization that owns shares in a company.
vocab.definition_zh: 股东；持有公司股份的个人或机构。
vocab.example_en: Shareholders asked the board for a clearer explanation.
vocab.example_zh: 股东要求董事会作出更清楚的解释。

vocab.definition_en: Relating to a generation, or exceptionally significant within a generation.
vocab.definition_zh: 一代人的；代际的；形容成就或企业时，也可指具有时代级影响力的。
vocab.example_en: The founder hopes to build a generational company.
vocab.example_zh: 这位创始人希望打造一家具有时代级影响力的公司。

vocab.definition_en: A main speech at an event that introduces or develops its central theme.
vocab.definition_zh: 主题演讲；大会上阐述核心议题的主要演讲。
vocab.example_en: Her keynote explored how coding agents could change software development.
vocab.example_zh: 她的主题演讲探讨了编程智能体可能如何改变软件开发。

vocab.definition_en: Unusual in an interesting or appealing way.
vocab.definition_zh: 古灵精怪的；独特而有趣的。
vocab.example_en: They built a quirky app that turns household chores into a game.
vocab.example_zh: 他们开发了一款古灵精怪的应用，把家务变成了游戏。

vocab.definition_en: To end a relationship, partnership, or working arrangement.
vocab.definition_zh: 分道扬镳；结束合作或雇佣关系。
vocab.example_en: The company and its designer agreed to part ways.
vocab.example_zh: 公司与设计师同意结束合作。

vocab.example_en: Many young engineers look up to her as a mentor.
vocab.example_zh: 许多年轻工程师都很敬佩她，把她视为导师。

quote.text_en: Well done is better than well said.
quote.author: Benjamin Franklin

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal expression apparently referring to a saved reset of a usage limit or quota. Its precise meaning depends on the product.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 非正式说法，在此似乎指攒下来的使用额度重置机会，具体机制取决于产品。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Anonymous or pseudonymous people online.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 网络上的匿名或使用化名的用户。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI systems that carry out programming tasks, often by editing code, using tools, and running checks.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 编程智能体；能够通过修改代码、调用工具和运行检查来执行编程任务的 AI 系统。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In AI, the observation associated with Rich Sutton that general methods leveraging computation ultimately outperform approaches built around human-provided knowledge.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: AI 领域的「苦涩的教训」，指 Rich Sutton 提出的观察，即充分利用计算能力的通用方法最终往往胜过依赖人工注入知识的方法。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI models with publicly available weights or other resources. Access and reuse conditions vary.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 开放模型；公开模型权重或其他资源的 AI 模型，具体访问和使用条件各不相同。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Public service announcement, often used online to introduce a helpful notice or reminder.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 公共服务公告的缩写，网络上常用来引出实用通知或提醒。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A positioning approach that strongly appeals to a target audience while openly putting off people who are a poor fit.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 一种定位策略，通过鲜明的立场或产品特点强烈吸引目标人群，同时让不匹配的人群主动远离。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In startup discussions, usually Request for Startups, a call for founders to build companies addressing particular problems.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 创业语境中通常指 Request for Startups，即公开征集解决特定问题的创业项目或创业团队。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A startup operating with limited public disclosure about its product or business.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 隐身模式；创业公司暂时对产品或业务细节保持低调、限制公开披露的状态。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Direct message, a private message on a social platform. Also used as a verb.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 私信，也可作动词，表示给某人发私信。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Open-source software, software distributed under a license permitting access to, modification of, and redistribution of its source code.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 开源软件；通过相应许可证允许查看、修改和再分发源代码的软件。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal expression for moving at the rapid speed associated with AI development.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 非正式表达，指以 AI 领域快速发展的节奏推进工作或迭代。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Subscription software designed for the specific needs of a particular industry.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 垂直行业 SaaS；针对某个特定行业需求提供的订阅制软件服务。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A company whose delivery model relies heavily on forward-deployed engineers working closely with customers to implement solutions.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 高度依赖前线部署工程师的公司，这些工程师深入客户场景，协助实施和定制解决方案。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In business, a strategy of acquiring and combining multiple companies into a larger group.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 商业语境中的并购整合策略，通过收购多家公司并将其组合为更大的企业集团。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A product serving a common need across multiple industries or business functions.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 横向通用产品；满足多个行业或业务职能共同需求的产品。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A playful adjective meaning related to or evocative of Codex, the AI coding tool.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 由 Codex 衍生出的玩笑式形容词，表示有 Codex 的感觉，或让人想使用 Codex。

slang_glossary.definition_en: So crowded that all seats are occupied and additional attendees must stand.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 座无虚席，后来的人只能站着，常用来形容活动人气很高。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The part of an email address after the @ symbol, often identifying the organization or email provider.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 邮箱域名，即电子邮件地址中 @ 后面的部分，通常标识所属组织或邮件服务商。

slang_glossary.definition_en: During a live internet broadcast.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在网络直播中。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for also known as, sometimes used humorously to introduce a reinterpretation.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: also known as 的缩写，表示「又称」，也常用于幽默地换一种说法。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal, milder substitute for a stronger swear word, used for emphasis.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 较温和的粗口替代词，用于加强惊讶、愤怒等语气。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal expression of strong surprise, confusion, or anger.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 表达强烈惊讶、困惑或愤怒的口语说法，类似「到底怎么回事」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal appeal expressing disbelief, frustration, or a request for someone to be reasonable.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 表达难以置信、不满或劝对方理智一点的口语说法，类似「拜托，哥们」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A game in which participants search for specified objects or complete tasks, often using clues.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 寻物游戏；参与者通常根据线索寻找指定物品或完成任务。
